newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX says tech problems delay move till July 7.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX says tech problems delay move till July 7.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) said Wednesday morning it was delaying its planned move to a new trading floor in New York City until July 7 from the previously scheduled date of May 27, traders said.
The announcement confirmed suspicions circulating since early Wednesday among traders, who had noted they had experienced numberous technical difficulties during mock trading sessions.

Other traders breathed a sigh of relief, saying the expiry next week of three of NYMEX's energy contracts would have lent trade at the new facility located on the northwest edge of New York's financial district a certain nightmarish quality.
June natural gas expires on Wednesday May 28, and June gasoline and heating oil expire on May 30.

NYMEX officials said the problems centered on certain phones, and that trade would continue until the move at the Exchange's current trading floor in New York's World Trade Center near the southern tip of Manhattan.
"We are just having a number of individual phone problems and we were told they would be resolved in time," a NYMEX official said.
"The phones are the lifeblood of the Exchange," said one trader, complaining NYMEX did not listen to concerns of the "rank-and-file" traders as it conceived and executed the move.
NYMEX said it delayed the move until July 7 because the Exchanged needs the three days over the U.S. Independence Day holiday weekend in the beginning of July to complete the move.
The upcoming three-day U.S. Memorial Day weekend would have afforded NYMEX the same long-weekend luxury.
